items.title: 67802_Charles Mingus oral history interview
items.q: For instance, (inaudible) like Clayton Powell, who looks like a white man, they were called elite.

ctx.x: See, I never fully understood that.
The blacks are not together, and they (inaudible) when I was a child. It was prejudiced against light skin, For instance, (inaudible) like Clayton Powell, who looks like a white man, they were

called elite. And they had the underground clan of the black who were school, in the knowledge of the history of the black people, the Africans, slaves, I never was taught anything about that, how they escaped. And they felt better (inaudible). So you call that the (highest) ECHELON of the black people. And they didn't associate with the common blacks, worked in labor and laborer or garbage men. Out in Watts, (inaudible) talking to guys whose parents weren't able to have an education, they couldn't hardly read or…
